summary: Trinidad and Tobago's Immigration Division publishes a list of countries whose citizens do not require visas for entry, among them Canada and the United Kingdom. The EU–Trinidad and Tobago agreement provides visa-free travel for citizens of the Union for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period and does not apply to Ireland, and an exchange of notes with South Korea lets each country's nationals enter without a visa for up to 90 days when not taking up paid activity. The Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs says a CARICOM national seeking to enter is granted a definite entry of six months, subject to all immigration requirements. Visas are applied for through the eVisa portal launched in April 2024, which replaced all previous and interim procedures; its FAQ says that to apply online you must be a foreign national from a country requiring a visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Trinidad and Tobago?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the countries on the Immigration Division's list of countries whose citizens do not require visas — among them Canada and the United Kingdom — need no visa. The EU–Trinidad and Tobago agreement provides visa-free travel for citizens of the Union for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period and does not apply to Ireland; an exchange of notes with South Korea lets each country's nationals enter without a visa for up to 90 days when not taking up paid activity. Some governments tell their own citizens: the US State Department says a tourist visa is required for stays longer than 90 days, Serbia's Foreign Ministry says Serbian passport holders do not need a visa for stays of up to 30 days, and Türkiye's Foreign Ministry says ordinary passport holders are visa-exempt for up to 30 days. A CARICOM national is granted a definite entry of six months, subject to all immigration requirements. Visas are applied for through the eVisa portal, whose FAQ says that to apply online you must be a foreign national from a country requiring a visa.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Trinidad and Tobago without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. The EU agreement allows a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period, and the exchange of notes with South Korea up to 90 days. The UK government tells British citizens they can visit without a visa for up to 90 days and can get the 90-day visit extended by applying to the passport and immigration department; the US State Department says a tourist visa is required for stays longer than 90 days; Serbia's and Türkiye's foreign ministries give 30 days. No official source we could read states a length of stay for the countries on the Immigration Division's no-visa list as a whole.

faq.question: What applies to CARICOM citizens?
faq.answer: Trinidad and Tobago's Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs says a CARICOM national seeking to enter Trinidad and Tobago is granted a definite entry of six months, subject to all immigration requirements. It says free movement of skills lets a CARICOM national seek work or engage in gainful employment in any participating CSME Member State (for free movement: Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, St. Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname and Trinidad and Tobago) without a work permit, and that holders of a CSME Skills Certificate not issued by Trinidad and Tobago must complete the verification process within six months of entry.

faq.question: Can Venezuelan citizens travel to Trinidad and Tobago visa-free?
faq.answer: Visa application instructions published by Trinidad and Tobago's Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs say that as of 17 June 2019 all Venezuelan nationals require a visa for entry into Trinidad and Tobago. The eVisa portal's FAQ says that to apply for a visa online you must be a foreign national from a country requiring a visa.
